defmodule Memba.OperationalAlerts.Worker do
  @moduledoc """
  Bounded asynchronous delivery for operational alerts on a single node.

  The caller does not deliver mail. It asks this GenServer to admit the alert;
  admission, dedupe, and in-flight limits are serialized in this process so
  concurrent callers cannot race. Delivery itself runs in supervised tasks.
  """

  use GenServer

  require Logger

  @task_supervisor Memba.OperationalAlerts.TaskSupervisor
  @dedupe_ttl_ms 60_000
  @max_in_flight 2

  def start_link(opts) do
    GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, opts, name: __MODULE__)
  end

  @impl GenServer
  def init(_opts) do
    {:ok, %{dedupe: %{}, in_flight: 0, monitors: %{}}}
  end

  def enqueue(alert, deliver_fun) when is_map(alert) and is_function(deliver_fun, 1) do
    if Process.whereis(__MODULE__) do
      GenServer.call(__MODULE__, {:enqueue, alert, deliver_fun})
    else
      :disabled
    end
  rescue
    error ->
      Logger.error("operational_alert_enqueue_failed error_module=#{safe_module(error)}")

      :dropped
  catch
    kind, _reason ->
      Logger.error("operational_alert_enqueue_failed failure_kind=#{kind}")
      :dropped
  end

  @impl GenServer
  def handle_call({:enqueue, alert, deliver_fun}, _from, state) do
    now = System.monotonic_time(:millisecond)
    state = expire_old_dedupe(state, now)
    signature = signature(alert)

    cond do
      Map.get(state.dedupe, signature, 0) > now ->
        {:reply, :deduplicated, state}

      state.in_flight >= @max_in_flight ->
        Logger.warning(
          "operational_alert_dropped reason=in_flight_limit kind=#{safe_kind(alert)}"
        )

        {:reply, :dropped, state}

      true ->
        case start_delivery_task(alert, deliver_fun) do
          {:ok, pid} ->
            ref = Process.monitor(pid)

            state = %{
              state
              | dedupe: Map.put(state.dedupe, signature, now + @dedupe_ttl_ms),
                in_flight: state.in_flight + 1,
                monitors: Map.put(state.monitors, ref, pid)
            }

            {:reply, :queued, state}

          {:error, reason} ->
            Logger.warning(
              "operational_alert_dropped reason=task_start_failed kind=#{safe_kind(alert)} failure_kind=#{failure_kind(reason)}"
            )

            {:reply, :dropped, state}
        end
    end
  end

  @impl GenServer
  def handle_info({:DOWN, ref, :process, _pid, reason}, state) do
    state =
      if Map.has_key?(state.monitors, ref) do
        if reason not in [:normal, :shutdown] do
          Logger.warning("operational_alert_task_exited reason_kind=#{failure_kind(reason)}")
        end

        %{
          state
          | in_flight: max(state.in_flight - 1, 0),
            monitors: Map.delete(state.monitors, ref)
        }
      else
        state
      end

    {:noreply, state}
  end

  defp start_delivery_task(alert, deliver_fun) do

defmodule Memba.OperationalAlerts do
  @moduledoc """
  Operator notifications for explicitly classified production technical failures.

  Alerting is disabled unless `:operational_alerts` supplies a destination.
  Payloads include release/request context and opaque Memba IDs only. They must
  not include free-text user input, email bodies, provider payloads, secrets, or
  full socket assigns.
  """

  import Swoosh.Email

  require Logger

  alias Memba.BuildInfo
  alias Memba.Mailer
  alias Memba.OperationalAlerts.Worker

  @app :memba
  @max_value_bytes 2_000
  @allowed_context_keys ~w(command command_ids event exception_kind exception_module module reason_kind request_id route transport view)a
  @allowed_string_context_keys MapSet.new(Enum.map(@allowed_context_keys, &Atom.to_string/1))

  def notify_liveview_crash(context) when is_map(context) do
    notify(:liveview_crash, context)
  end

  @doc """
  Explicitly alert on a technical command failure.

  Do not use this for expected domain, validation, duplicate, or ordinary
  authorization results. Call sites must classify the failure as technical first
  (for example, projection/aggregate authorization-state disagreement).
  """
  def notify_command_failure(command, reason, context \\ %{}) do
    context =
      context
      |> safe_map()
      |> Map.put(:command, inspect(command.__struct__))
      |> Map.put(:command_ids, command_ids(command))
      |> Map.merge(safe_reason_context(reason))

    notify(:command_failure, context)
  end

  def send_test_alert(context \\ %{}) when is_map(context) do
    notify(:controlled_test, Map.put(context, :reason, "controlled operator alert test"))
  end

  def notify(kind, context) when is_atom(kind) and is_map(context) do
    if configured?() do
      alert = alert_payload(kind, context)
      result = Worker.enqueue(alert, &deliver/1)

      if result == :queued do
        Logger.error("operational_alert_queued #{Jason.encode!(alert)}",
          event: "operational_alert_queued",
          alert_kind: Atom.to_string(kind),
          git_sha: alert.release.git_sha,
          request_id: alert.request_id
        )
      end

      result
    else
      :disabled
    end
  rescue
    error ->
      Logger.error("operational_alert_failed error_module=#{safe_module(error)}")
      :dropped
  catch
    kind, _reason ->
      Logger.error("operational_alert_failed failure_kind=#{kind}")
      :dropped
  end

  def configured? do
    enabled?() and configured_to() not in [nil, ""] and configured_from() not in [nil, ""]
  end
